name: HomeBoost (BoostBox)
key_features: DIY home energy assessment kit; Thermal camera that plugs into an iPhone; Blacklight; Guided app scan (about 30 minutes); Report of upgrades and rebates
strengths: All-in $99 kit costs less than buying a FLIR ONE ($149.99-$199.99); Available nationwide; Keep the kit or mail it back; Head start (launched Oct 2024)
weaknesses: Kit camera plugs into iPhones; Built around its own kit rather than cameras people already own or borrow from libraries; Funding not public

name: FLIR ONE (Gen 3 / Pro)
key_features: Clip-on thermal camera; MSX imaging; FLIR ONE app; FLIR Mobile SDK for approved third-party apps
strengths: Brand recognition; Accurate imaging; Pro-grade features; Makes the FLIR ONE hardware this product runs on
weaknesses: Expensive ($149.99-$399.99); FLIR ONE app shows raw thermal images with little guidance; Steep learning curve

name: Seek Thermal
key_features: Smartphone thermal camera; Multiple models; App included
strengths: Low-cost entry model (Nano 200 at $149); Good resolution; Easy to use
weaknesses: Nano has no third-party SDK (only Seek's Nano app), so this product cannot support it at launch; Limited analysis features; No guidance

name: Home Energy Saver (DOE)
key_features: Free audit tool; Recommendations; Utility integration
weaknesses: Not visual/thermal; Requires manual data entry; Generic advice

name: Energy Star Home Advisor
key_features: DIY assessment; Improvement calculator; Rebate finder
weaknesses: No thermal imaging; Manual inspection; Basic

name: Local Energy Auditors
key_features: Professional assessment; Blower door test; Detailed report
strengths: Thorough; Expert interpretation; Sometimes required for rebates

name: Sense Home Energy Monitor
key_features: Electrical monitoring; Real-time tracking; Device detection
strengths: Continuous monitoring; Good UX; Smart home integration
weaknesses: Different approach (electrical vs thermal); Installation required; Higher cost

name: Emporia Vue
key_features: Circuit-level monitoring; Low cost; Real-time app
weaknesses: Limited to electrical; No thermal/leak detection; Requires some DIY
